title: Appointment slot booking
when: The user wants a page where clients pick a service, a day and a free time slot and confirm a booking, stored locally with no server.

title: Brick breaker paddle and ball game
when: The user wants the arcade game where a paddle bounces a ball to break rows of bricks, with lives, levels and score.

title: Budget tracker for income, expenses and categories
when: The user wants to record income and expenses by category and month, see the balance and how spending compares to a monthly budget.

title: Calculator with keyboard input
when: The user wants a working calculator app with a keypad, chained operations, percent, sign change and keyboard support.

title: Chat interface with local echo replies
when: The user wants a chat screen with message bubbles, an input bar and replies, working offline with a local echo or scripted bot and no server.

title: Color sequence memory game
when: The user wants the game where colored pads light up in a growing sequence and the player repeats it.

title: Contact book with groups, search and export
when: The user wants an address book app to store people with phone, email and notes, search them and export contacts.

title: Countdown to a date or event
when: The user wants a countdown showing days, hours, minutes and seconds until an event, launch, birthday or deadline.

title: Records manager with create, edit, delete and search
when: The user wants a small app to register and manage records (clients, students, products, members) with a form, a searchable table, edit and delete.

title: Currency converter with stored exchange rates
when: The user wants to convert amounts between currencies offline, using a local rates file or rates the user enters, with the rate date visible.

title: Analytics dashboard from a local JSON file
when: The user wants a dashboard with KPI cards, charts and a table built from a local JSON data file, filtered by date or category.

title: Dice roller with notation and history
when: The user wants to roll virtual dice, from a quick d6 to role playing notation like 2d6+3 or 4d6 keep highest 3, with a history.

title: Drawing canvas app with brush, eraser and undo
when: The user wants a paint or sketch app to draw with mouse, pen or finger, pick colors and sizes, undo and save the picture.

title: Group expense splitter that settles who owes whom
when: The user wants to split shared costs of a trip, house or dinner among friends and get the shortest list of payments to settle up.

title: Flashcards with spaced repetition
when: The user wants flashcards to study vocabulary or facts, where missed cards return sooner and known cards later.

title: Four in a row disc drop game
when: The user wants the vertical grid game where players drop discs into columns and try to line up four, against a friend or the computer.

title: Guess the number game
when: The user wants the classic game where the computer picks a secret number and the player guesses with higher or lower hints.

title: Habit tracker with streaks and a weekly grid
when: The user wants to track daily habits, tick them off each day and see current and longest streaks.

title: Hangman word game
when: The user wants hangman: guess a hidden word letter by letter before running out of misses.

title: Image filters with Canvas
when: The user wants to open a photo in the browser, apply filters such as grayscale, sepia, brightness, contrast or blur, and download the result.

title: Inventory tracker with stock movements and low stock alerts
when: The user wants to track product stock with incoming and outgoing movements, minimum levels and alerts for low stock.

title: Kanban board with drag and keyboard moves
when: The user wants a kanban or task board with columns and cards that move by drag and drop and by keyboard, saved locally.

title: Loan payment calculator with amortization schedule
when: The user wants to compute the monthly payment, total interest and payoff schedule of a loan, mortgage or financing, with optional extra payments.

title: Markdown editor with live, escaped preview
when: The user wants a Markdown editor with a side by side live preview, a formatting toolbar and download of the result.

title: Notes app with Markdown, search and autosave
when: The user wants a notes app: a list of notes, an editor, search and autosave in the browser, with simple Markdown formatting in the view mode.

title: Maze game with generated levels
when: The user wants a maze game: generated mazes that the player walks through with keys or swipes to reach the exit, growing level by level.

title: Memory card matching game
when: The user wants a memory game where cards are flipped two at a time to find matching pairs, with moves and time counted.

title: Metronome with Web Audio scheduling
when: The user wants a metronome with adjustable tempo, time signature, accented first beat and tap tempo.

title: Hidden mines grid game with flags
when: The user wants the classic grid of hidden mines: reveal cells, numbers count nearby mines, flag suspects, clear every safe cell to win.

title: Month calendar view with events
when: The user wants a month calendar grid to browse months and add, edit and delete events on days.

title: Music playlist player with the audio element
when: The user wants a music player with a playlist, play and pause, next and previous, seek, volume, shuffle and repeat.

title: Random name picker wheel
when: The user wants a spinning wheel or picker that chooses a random name or option from a list, for raffles, classrooms or decisions.

title: Password generator with strength estimate
when: The user wants a tool that generates strong random passwords or passphrases with options for length and character sets.

title: Poll and voting app with live results
when: The user wants to create a poll with options, let people vote and show results as percentages and bars.

title: Focus timer with work and break cycles
when: The user wants a focus timer that alternates work sessions with short and long breaks, with start, pause, skip and a sound at the end.

title: Multiple choice quiz with score and review
when: The user wants a quiz or trivia app: questions with choices, feedback after each answer, a score at the end and a review of mistakes.

title: Reading list with status, progress and ratings
when: The user wants to keep a list of books to read, reading and finished, with page progress, ratings and a yearly goal.

title: Recipe box with ingredient scaling
when: The user wants an app to save their own recipes, search them by name or ingredient, and scale ingredient amounts to a number of servings.

title: Rock paper scissors against the computer
when: The user wants rock paper scissors against the computer, with rounds, a match score and maybe a computer that adapts.

title: Shopping list grouped by aisle
when: The user wants a grocery or shopping list to use in the store: quick add, grouped by aisle, tick items as bought.

title: Sliding number tiles merge puzzle
when: The user wants the 4x4 puzzle where all tiles slide in one direction and equal numbers merge into their double, with score and undo.

title: Snake game on a canvas grid
when: The user wants the classic snake game: the snake moves on a grid, eats food to grow, and the game ends on hitting a wall or itself.

title: Stopwatch with laps and split times
when: The user wants a stopwatch with start, stop, reset and lap times, showing hundredths and the fastest and slowest laps.

title: Sudoku puzzle with notes and checking
when: The user wants a playable sudoku with puzzles by difficulty, pencil notes, conflict highlighting and hints.

title: Two paddle table tennis game
when: The user wants the retro two paddle ball game, for two players on one keyboard or against a computer paddle.

title: Tap to fly side scroller
when: The user wants a one button game where each tap lifts a flying character through gaps in moving obstacles, scoring per gap.

title: Tic tac toe with an unbeatable or easy computer
when: The user wants tic tac toe for two players or against the computer, with a hard mode that never loses and an easy mode for kids.

title: Time tracker for projects and tasks
when: The user wants to start and stop a timer per project or task, edit entries and see daily and weekly totals of hours, maybe with earnings.

title: Tip calculator with bill split per person
when: The user wants a quick tip calculator: bill amount, tip percent and number of people, giving the tip, total and amount per person.

title: Todo list app with filters and saved tasks
when: The user wants a todo list, task list or checklist app to add, check off, edit and delete tasks that stay after a reload.

title: Typing speed test with WPM and accuracy
when: The user wants a typing test that measures words per minute and accuracy over a timed passage.

title: Unit converter for length, weight, temperature and more
when: The user wants to convert measurements between units such as meters and feet, kilograms and pounds, Celsius and Fahrenheit, liters and gallons.

title: Weather card from a local JSON file
when: The user wants a weather widget or page showing current conditions and a short forecast, read from a local JSON file instead of a live service.

title: Whack a mole reflex game
when: The user wants a reflex game where moles pop out of holes for short moments and the player hits them for points before time runs out.

title: Five letter word guessing game
when: The user wants the daily word puzzle: six tries to guess a five letter word, each guess scored letter by letter as right spot, in the word, or absent.

title: Accessible charts with a data table fallback
when: Any page that shows a chart, or a review of an existing chart for accessibility.

title: Data model design for an app
when: Before building an app that stores records (tasks, orders, members, bookings), or when the data shape is messy and needs a redesign.

title: Backup and restore app data to a JSON file
when: A browser app keeps data locally (localStorage or IndexedDB) and users need to back it up, move it to another device or recover it.

title: Calendar heatmap of daily activity
when: The user wants a year or months view of daily counts (habits, workouts, commits, sales per day) as colored squares.

title: Export data as a CSV download
when: The user wants a button that downloads table or list data as a CSV file that opens correctly in spreadsheet programs.

title: CSV parser that handles quotes and line breaks
when: JavaScript code must read CSV text (from a file input, a fetch or Node) where fields can hold commas, quotes or line breaks.

title: Cleaning and normalizing messy data
when: Imported or typed data has stray spaces, mixed case, different number or date formats, empty markers or variant spellings.

title: Dates and time zones with Intl
when: The app shows, stores or compares dates and times, schedules across time zones, or dates appear one day off.

title: Finding and merging duplicate records
when: A list has repeated people, products or entries (after imports or merges) and the user wants them found and combined.

title: Import a JSON or CSV file with a file input
when: The user wants to load data from a file on their computer into a web app (contacts, transactions, a saved project) without a server.

title: Client side form validation with clear errors
when: A form must check fields before submit and show helpful, accessible errors (sign up, checkout, contact, settings).

title: Fuzzy search with typo tolerance and ranking
when: Exact search is not enough: users misspell names, type abbreviations, or need ranked suggestions for autocomplete or a command palette.

title: Geographic distance and nearest places
when: The app must compute distances between coordinates, sort places by distance, or find everything within a radius.

title: Histogram with sensible bins
when: The user wants to see how values are distributed (ages, response times, prices, scores) rather than compare categories.

title: Generating ids with crypto.randomUUID
when: Records created in the browser or Node need unique ids, or the code uses Date.now(), counters or Math.random for ids.

title: Locale aware sorting with Intl.Collator
when: Names, titles or files must sort alphabetically the way people expect: accents in place, case ignored, item 2 before item 10.

title: Joining and merging two datasets
when: Data from two sources must be combined by a shared key (orders with customers, prices with products, two exports of one list).

title: Reshaping JSON: group, index and summarize
when: Data must be grouped, totaled, indexed by id, flattened or nested differently before display or export.

title: Search, filter and sort a list
when: The user has a list or table (products, contacts, tasks) and wants a search box, filter controls and sortable columns.

title: localStorage persistence with schema version and migration
when: A browser app saves settings or data in localStorage and must survive reloads, storage errors and future changes to its data shape.

title: Parsing and summarizing log files
when: The user has server or app log files and wants errors counted, slow requests found, or a summary report.

title: Safe small Markdown to HTML converter
when: An app must render user written Markdown (notes, comments, a preview pane) as HTML without external libraries.

title: Money in integer cents
when: The app adds prices, applies discounts or taxes, splits bills or totals invoices, and results like 0.1 + 0.2 must never appear.

title: Nice axis ticks and scales
when: A chart needs axis ticks at round, human friendly values, or labels come out like 13.7, 27.4, 41.1.

title: Formatting numbers, currency and units with Intl
when: The app shows prices, totals, percentages, large counts or measurements and they must look right for the user locale.

title: Offline queue that syncs when back online
when: Users make changes offline or on a bad connection and those changes must reach a server later, without loss or duplicates.

title: Pagination for long lists
when: A list or API result is too long to show at once and needs pages, page numbers or cursor based paging.

title: Parsing date strings safely
when: Dates arrive as text (CSV imports, typed input, old records) in formats like 17/10/2026, 2026-10-17 or 10/17/2026 and must become reliable values.

title: Personal data minimization and privacy by design
when: An app or form collects names, emails, phones, locations, health or payment details, or a review asks whether personal data is handled well.

title: Small state store with subscribe
when: Several parts of a vanilla JavaScript app need the same data and must update together when it changes.

title: Realistic seed and demo data
when: An app needs believable demo content, test fixtures, or enough records to see how lists, charts and paging behave.

title: Hand written schema validation for JSON data
when: Data from storage, imports or API requests must be checked against an expected shape at runtime, without a validation library.

title: Sparklines inside tables and cards
when: A table, list or stat card needs a tiny trend line next to a number (last 30 days, recent prices).

title: Summary statistics: mean, median, percentiles
when: The user wants averages, medians, percentiles, spread or outliers over a list of numbers (times, prices, scores).

title: Bar chart in plain SVG
when: The user wants to compare values across categories (sales by month, votes per option, top products) as bars, without a chart library.

title: Donut chart for parts of a whole
when: The user wants to show how a total splits into a few parts (budget by category, survey answers, disk usage).

title: Line chart for trends over time
when: Values change over time (daily visits, weight, temperature, balance) and the user wants to see the trend.

title: Chart generated from an HTML table
when: A page already has a data table, or the content belongs in a table, and the user wants a chart of it without duplicating the numbers.

title: Undo and redo history
when: An editor, drawing tool, form builder or list app needs Undo and Redo with buttons and keyboard shortcuts.

title: Reusable validator functions
when: The same rules (required, length, email, range, date) are needed in several forms, or in both the page and a Node server.

title: Brand palette built from one color
when: The user has one brand or logo color and wants a full set of shades, matching neutrals and status colors around it.

title: Breakpoint strategy for responsive layouts
when: The user wants a plan for responsive design (which breakpoints, mobile first rules) or a layout that breaks at odd widths.

title: Button hierarchy: primary, secondary, tertiary
when: The user wants consistent button styles, or a screen has several actions competing for attention.

title: Color palette with WCAG AA contrast
when: The user wants a color palette, color scheme or theme colors for a page or app, with text that stays readable.

title: Corner radius scale and consistency
when: The user wants rounded corners consistent across buttons, inputs, cards and images, or has picked a soft or sharp look.

title: Dark color palette that stays readable
when: The user wants a dark look or dark theme colors and needs surfaces, text and accents that read well without glare.

title: Data visualization color palettes
when: The user builds charts, graphs, maps or dashboards and needs colors for series, ranges or positive and negative values.

title: Design consistency audit of a stylesheet
when: The design looks slightly off everywhere and the user wants inconsistent colors, sizes, spacing and radii found and unified.

title: Structured design critique of a page
when: The user asks for feedback on how a page or screen looks and works, and wants a clear list of what to change.

title: Design tokens as CSS custom properties
when: The user wants a token file or a small design system: named values for color, type, space, radius, shadow and motion.

title: Elevation scale with layered shadows
when: The user wants cards, menus, dialogs and sticky bars to look layered, or current shadows look muddy and inconsistent.

title: Error, offline and failure state design
when: The user needs designed screens and inline states for when loading, saving or connecting fails, instead of a blank or broken area.

title: Fluid typography with clamp
when: The user wants headings and text that scale smoothly between phone and desktop instead of jumping at breakpoints.

title: System font stacks and font pairing
when: The user wants to choose fonts, pair a heading font with a body font, or use fast system fonts with no downloads.

title: Form layout and field design
when: The user wants a form to look and read well: labels, field widths, help text, grouping, error look and the submit area.

title: Site header and logo placement
when: The user wants a site header designed: where the logo goes, how big, how nav and actions line up, sticky or not.

title: Icons with an inline SVG sprite
when: The user wants icons in buttons, menus, lists or beside labels, without an icon font or any download.

title: Image aspect ratios and object-fit
when: Images in cards, galleries or heroes have mixed shapes, look stretched, or make the layout jump while loading.

title: Auto fit card grid without media queries
when: The user wants a grid of cards, products, photos or features that adapts its column count to the screen width.

title: Bento grid of feature tiles
when: The user wants a bento box section: tiles of different sizes showing features, stats or images in a tight mosaic.

title: Centered content column with full bleed breakouts
when: The user wants page content centered in a readable column while some bands, maps or images run the full width.

title: Holy grail layout with CSS grid areas
when: The user wants a page with header, footer, a main column and one or two side columns such as navigation and related links.

title: Magazine style editorial layout
when: The user wants a news, magazine or editorial front page with a lead story, secondary stories and headline lists.

title: Sidebar and content layout that wraps
when: The user wants a sidebar (filters, menu, profile) beside fluid content that drops below it on narrow screens.

title: Split hero with text and image side by side
when: The user wants a hero section with the message on one side and an image, illustration or short form on the other.

title: Sticky footer on short pages
when: The footer floats mid screen on short pages and the user wants it at the bottom of the window without covering content.

title: Readable line length and vertical rhythm
when: Long text (articles, docs, policies) feels hard to read, or the user wants steady spacing between paragraphs, headings and lists.

title: Loading feedback: skeletons, spinners, progress
when: The user wants to show that something is loading, saving or processing, and must choose a spinner, a skeleton or a progress bar.

title: Hover and press micro interactions
when: The user wants buttons, cards and links to feel responsive with hover, press, toggle and copied or saved feedback.

title: Choosing a mobile navigation pattern
when: The user asks how navigation should work on phones: hamburger, bottom tab bar, priority plus, or a simple link row.

title: Motion design that respects reduced motion
when: The user wants animations or transitions (reveals, fades, sliding panels) and they must stay comfortable for everyone.

title: Multiple color themes with data-theme
when: The user wants several themes (light, dark, high contrast, seasonal or brand variants) that visitors can pick.

title: Semantic color tokens for UI states
when: The user needs consistent colors for meaning (success, warning, danger, info, selected, disabled) across messages, badges and inputs.

title: Spacing scale on a 4 or 8 px grid
when: The user wants consistent padding, margins and gaps, or says the layout feels uneven, cramped or random.

title: Living style guide page
when: The user wants one page that shows the design system: colors, type, spacing, buttons, forms and components with their states.

title: Touch target size and focus rings
when: Controls are hard to tap on phones or keyboard focus is invisible, and the user wants comfortable, visible targets.

title: Typography scale for headings and text
when: The user wants consistent font sizes, heading sizes or a type system for a page or app.

title: UI microcopy: labels, buttons and messages
when: The user wants the small words of an interface written well: buttons, field labels, hints, confirmations, errors and tooltips.

title: Visual direction from brand personality
when: The user describes a feeling (playful, premium, trustworthy, rustic) and wants it turned into concrete visual choices before building.

title: Visual hierarchy for a screen
when: A page or screen feels flat or busy and the user wants the important things to stand out in the right order.

title: Whitespace and grouping by proximity
when: The layout looks cluttered or cramped, or boxes and divider lines are used everywhere to separate content.

title: Low fidelity wireframe before styling
when: Before building a page or app the user wants the structure agreed first: a grayscale wireframe of sections and content blocks.

title: HTTP API reference documentation
when: The user wants reference documentation for an HTTP API: endpoints, parameters, request and response bodies, errors.

title: Architecture decision record (ADR)
when: The team made or must make a significant technical choice and the user wants it documented with context and tradeoffs.

title: Split work into atomic commits
when: A working copy has many mixed changes and the user wants them committed as a clean series of focused commits.

title: Git branching workflow
when: The user or team wants a simple, written branching model for daily work, releases and hotfixes.

title: Write a clear bug report
when: The user found a problem and wants it written up as an issue that someone else can reproduce and fix.

title: CHANGELOG entry
when: The user wants to record changes for a new version, or start a CHANGELOG for the project.

title: CLI --help text
when: A command line tool needs a clear --help output and usage error messages.

title: When and how to write code comments
when: The user asks to comment code, explain tricky parts in the source, or clean up noisy or outdated comments.

title: Commit message
when: The user asks for a commit message, or work is ready to commit and needs a clear description of the change.

title: Configuration reference docs
when: The user wants every configuration option of an app or tool documented in one reference page.

title: CONTRIBUTING guide
when: The user wants contributors to know how to set up, change, test and submit work to the project.

title: Docstrings for Python and public functions
when: The user wants each public function, class or module documented in place with docstrings or doc comments.

title: FAQ document
when: The user wants a FAQ for a project, product or service, written as a Markdown document.

title: Write a feature request
when: The user wants to propose a new feature or improvement in a way that maintainers can evaluate and plan.

title: Getting started tutorial
when: The user wants a step by step tutorial that takes a beginner from nothing to a first working result with the project.

title: Find the commit that broke it with git bisect
when: Something worked in an older version and is broken now, and the user wants to find the commit that introduced it.

title: Undo and recover from git mistakes
when: The user committed the wrong thing, lost work, committed to the wrong branch, or wants to undo a pushed change.

title: Set up .gitignore
when: A new repository needs a .gitignore, or generated, local or secret files keep showing up in git status.

title: Explain license options for a project
when: The user wants to choose or add a license for a project and needs the common options explained, without legal advice.

title: Resolve merge conflicts
when: A merge, rebase or pull stopped with conflicts and the user needs them resolved correctly.

title: Migration guide between versions
when: A new major version changes APIs, config or data, and users need step by step instructions to upgrade.

title: Pull request description
when: The user opens a pull request or merge request and needs a description, or asks to summarize a branch for reviewers.

title: README for a command line tool
when: The project is a command line tool or script and the user wants its README with install, usage and options.

title: Library README with API section
when: The project is a reusable module or library and the user wants a README that documents its public API.

title: Project README
when: The user wants a README for a project, app or site, or the existing README is missing, outdated or vague.

title: Release notes for users
when: The user wants announcement style notes for a release, for users or customers rather than developers.

title: Tag a release with semantic versioning
when: The user is ready to release a version and needs the right version number, the tag and the files updated.

title: Reply to code review comments
when: The user received review comments on a change and wants to respond to each and update the code.

title: SECURITY.md vulnerability policy
when: The user wants a security policy that tells people how to report vulnerabilities and what to expect.

title: Troubleshooting guide
when: The user wants a document that helps users diagnose and fix common errors with a project on their own.

title: Writing acceptance criteria
when: A plan needs the list of conditions QA will test, or the brief has goals but nothing a checker can say yes or no to.

title: Handling a change request mid job
when: The user asks for a change while the crew is already working: a new feature, a different color, a removed page.

title: Asking the right clarifying questions, three at most
when: A request is missing information that would change the files, and the foreman may ask the user before planning.

title: Keeping a decision log
when: The crew makes choices that later workers or the user might question: storage, file layout, a library free approach, a dropped feature.

title: Definition of done for a crew job
when: The crew needs one shared finish line for a job: when to stop adding, when QA can pass, when the user gets the result.

title: Estimating task size for the crew
when: The foreman must judge whether a task fits one worker run, or the user asks how big or how long a job is.

title: Identifying risks before work starts
when: A job has unknowns: a tricky algorithm, existing files that must not break, data from the user, or limits of the local model.

title: Milestones for a larger project
when: The request is too big for one crew job, so it must be split into milestones that each end with something usable.

title: One task per file: file ownership
when: Two workers could touch the same file, or a plan has tasks that edit one file from several sides.

title: Ordering tasks by dependencies
when: A plan has several tasks and the foreman must set what runs first and what can run side by side.

title: Planning accessibility from the start
when: Any job with a user interface, so that accessibility is built into tasks instead of patched after QA.

title: Planning a small browser game
when: The user asks for a game (puzzle, arcade, word or card game) and the crew must plan it so it is playable at the end of the job.

title: Planning a bug investigation
when: The user reports that something is broken and the cause is unknown, so the crew must plan how to find it before fixing.

title: Planning a data migration
when: Stored data must change shape: a new field, a renamed key, CSV to JSON, or a new localStorage version, without losing records.

title: Planning the documentation for a job
when: A job produces something people must open, run, configure or maintain, and the plan must decide which docs to write.

title: Planning for small local models
when: The crew runs on a small local model with a short context window, and plans must stay inside what such a model can do reliably.

title: Task plan for a site with several pages
when: The foreman plans a website with three or more pages and must split it among workers without inconsistent headers or styles.

title: Planning a safe refactor
when: The user wants existing code reorganized (split a big file, rename, remove duplication) without changing what it does.

title: Planning a small local API
when: The user wants a small HTTP API or local server (node:http) and the crew must agree on routes and data before coding.

title: Planning which tests to write
when: A job contains logic (calculations, parsing, state changes, routes) and the plan must say which tests exist and who writes them.

title: Prioritizing with must, should, could
when: A request lists many features or the crew has more ideas than turns, and work must be ranked before planning.

title: Recovering when a task fails
when: A task failed QA or review more than once, a worker got stuck, or a city task is near its loop limit and about to be blocked.

title: Extracting requirements from a conversation
when: Requirements are scattered across a long chat, pasted messages or notes, and the crew needs one clean brief before planning.

title: Reviewing a plan before work starts
when: A plan is drafted and should be checked once before the crew spends turns on it.

title: Scoping a first version
when: The request describes a large product and the crew must choose what the first delivery contains.

title: Split a request into small tasks
when: A new request arrives and the foreman must turn it into a list of tasks for the crew before anyone writes a file.

title: Staffing the crew: who does what
when: The plan has tasks and the foreman must choose an assignee for each from the available workers and hired agents.

title: Defining success measures for a result
when: The user states a goal beyond the files (more bookings, faster checkout, fewer support questions) and the plan should say how to tell it worked.

title: Timeboxing work in turns
when: A task could grow without end (research, polish, debugging) and the plan must cap it with a budget and a stop rule.

title: Comparing options with a tradeoff table
when: There are two to four real ways to build something (storage, layout, file split, approach) and the crew must pick one with reasons.

title: Writing user stories for a job
when: The request describes what people want to do, and the plan should capture it as stories that guide tasks and criteria.

title: Detecting a vague request and stating assumptions
when: The request is one line or very open ("make an app", "a site for my business") and the crew must decide how to read it.

title: Accessibility audit and fixes
when: The user asks to check or improve the accessibility of a page or app, or to meet WCAG.

title: Accessible names and labels for screen readers
when: Controls, icons, images or links are announced badly or not at all by screen readers, or forms lack labels.

title: Add types with JSDoc
when: The user wants type safety or editor hints in plain JavaScript without a compile step.

title: Add unit tests with node:test
when: The user wants unit tests added for existing functions, calculations or modules, using only the Node standard library (or unittest in Python).

title: Speed up slow loops and algorithms
when: A script or function is slow on larger data, a loop takes seconds, or the page freezes while processing.

title: Consistent API error responses
when: An HTTP API returns errors in mixed shapes (strings, stack traces, 200 with error) and clients cannot handle them reliably.

title: Fix async race conditions
when: Results flicker or show old data, a double click submits twice, or async calls finish in a different order than they started.

title: Validate input at system boundaries
when: Data enters the program from a form, a request body, a file, storage or command line arguments and must be checked.

title: Fix a bug from an error message and stack trace
when: The user pastes an error, exception, traceback or crash report, or says something throws, and wants it fixed.

title: Clean up console errors and warnings
when: The browser console or Node output shows errors, warnings or leftover debug logs that the user wants gone.

title: Fix color contrast
when: Text or controls are hard to read, a check reports low contrast, or the user wants colors to meet WCAG AA.

title: Configuration management
when: Settings are hard coded or scattered, or the app needs different values per environment or per user.

title: Make code style consistent
when: Files mix quote styles, indentation, naming and module patterns, and the user wants one consistent style without new tools.

title: Content Security Policy for a site
when: The user wants to harden a site against injected scripts, add security headers, or a policy is blocking parts of the page.

title: Fix broken CSS layout and overflow
when: Elements overlap, a page scrolls sideways, text spills out of cards, or flex and grid items do not line up.

title: Dark mode for an existing site
when: The user wants an existing site or app to get a dark version that follows the system setting, with every component readable in it.

title: Migrate stored data to a new format
when: The shape of saved data changes (localStorage, IndexedDB, JSON files) and existing users must keep their data.

title: Debounce and throttle frequent events
when: A handler runs on every keystroke, scroll or resize and causes lag, too many requests, or repeated saves.

title: Debug a failing test
when: A test fails or broke after a change and the user wants to know whether the code or the test is wrong, and fix it.

title: Deprecate APIs with backward compatibility
when: A function, option, endpoint or file format must change and existing users should keep working while they migrate.

title: Batch DOM updates and avoid reflow
when: Rendering a list or updating many elements makes the page stutter, scrolling is janky, or a table with many rows renders slowly.

title: Write tests for edge cases
when: Tests exist for the happy path and the user wants coverage of tricky inputs: empty, huge, invalid, boundary or unusual values.

title: Error handling strategy for an app
when: The user wants consistent error handling across an app or script: where to catch, what to throw, how to report.

title: Fix event listeners that do not fire
when: A click, submit, input or key handler does nothing, fires twice, or stops working after the list re-renders.

title: Feature flags for gradual changes
when: The user wants to ship a feature hidden, turn it on for some users, or keep a quick off switch for risky code.

title: Safe file upload handling
when: The app lets users upload images, documents or CSV files, in the browser only or to a Node server.

title: Manage focus in dynamic interfaces
when: Content opens, closes or changes without a page load (dialogs, route changes, deleted items, inline errors) and focus gets lost.

title: Graceful shutdown for Node servers
when: A Node server or worker must stop cleanly on Ctrl+C, restarts or deploys without dropping requests or corrupting files.

title: HTTP caching headers
when: A Node server serves static files or API responses and the user wants faster repeat loads or sees stale files after updates.

title: Extract strings for translation (i18n)
when: The user wants the app or site available in more than one language, or to move hard coded text into translation files.

title: Prevent command, SQL and path traversal injection
when: Server or script code builds shell commands, SQL queries or file paths from user input, or the user wants an injection review.

title: Fix keyboard navigation
when: Parts of a page cannot be used with the keyboard, tab order jumps around, or custom widgets ignore Enter, Space or arrow keys.

title: Log levels and redacting sensitive data
when: Logs are too noisy or too quiet, or may contain passwords, tokens, emails or other personal data.

title: Find and fix memory leaks
when: An app gets slower or uses more memory the longer it runs, or a long running Node process grows until it crashes.

title: Keep dependencies minimal
when: A project pulls in packages for small tasks, the user wants fewer dependencies, or must run with no installs.

title: Build a minimal reproduction of a bug
when: A bug is intermittent, depends on a big app, or must be reported, and the user wants the smallest case that shows it.

title: Modernize legacy JavaScript
when: Old JavaScript uses var, callbacks, prototype classes, global scripts or XMLHttpRequest and the user wants modern syntax.

title: Fix money and floating point rounding errors
when: Totals show values like 0.30000000000000004, prices are off by a cent, or sums do not match between screens.

title: Fix "is not a function" errors
when: The error says something "is not a function", or a call fails because the value is undefined, a string, or an object.

title: Fix null or undefined property access
when: Code crashes reading a property of null or undefined, such as a missing element, an empty API field or an unset variable.

title: Find and fix off by one errors
when: Results are missing the first or last item, a loop runs one time too many, pages overlap, or dates are a day off.

title: Improve page load performance
when: A web page loads slowly, shows content late, shifts while loading, or the user asks to make the site faster.

title: Password storage and session basics
when: The user builds sign up and login on a Node server and needs passwords and sessions handled safely.

title: Plurals, numbers, dates and currency formatting
when: Text shows "1 items", dates or prices appear in the wrong format for the language, or numbers need locale aware output.

title: Progressive enhancement
when: The user wants pages that work when scripts fail or load slowly, with script adding extras on top of working HTML.

title: Extract function refactor
when: The user asks to refactor a long or repeated block of code into smaller named functions without changing behavior.

title: Remove dead and unused code
when: The user wants to clean a project of unused functions, variables, files, CSS rules or commented out blocks.

title: Rename variables and functions for clarity
when: The user says the code is hard to read because of vague names (data, tmp, x, handle2) and wants better naming.

title: Fix responsive layout on phones at 375 px
when: A page looks wrong on a phone: tiny text, cut off content, sideways scroll, crowded menus or unusable buttons.

title: Responsive images with srcset and sizes
when: Images are heavy on phones, blurry on high density screens, or the user wants modern formats with fallbacks.

title: REST API conventions
when: The user designs or cleans up an HTTP JSON API and wants consistent URLs, methods, status codes and pagination.

title: Retries with exponential backoff
when: Network or file operations fail now and then and the user wants automatic retries without hammering the other side.

title: Right to left language support
when: The site must support Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu, or mixed direction text displays in the wrong order.

title: Handle secrets and API keys safely
when: Code contains keys, passwords or tokens, the user needs to configure credentials, or wants a review for leaked secrets.

title: Security review for XSS
when: The user asks for a security review of web code, or the app shows user supplied or fetched text on the page.

title: SEO basics for a site
when: The user wants a site to show up and look good in search results and link previews.

title: Fix bugs from shared mutable state
when: Changing one object or array unexpectedly changes another, defaults leak between calls, or state updates do not show.

title: Sitemap and robots.txt
when: The user wants search engines to find all pages of a site, or to keep some pages out of search results.

title: Split a large file into modules
when: A single script has grown into hundreds of lines and the user wants it organized into several modules.

title: Add structured data with JSON-LD
when: The user wants rich search results for a business, product, article, event, recipe or FAQ page.

title: Structured logging for Node services
when: A server or script logs with scattered console.log calls and the user wants logs that can be searched and filtered.

title: Make DOM code testable by splitting pure logic
when: Browser code mixes calculations with DOM updates and the user wants tests that run in Node without a browser.

title: Timeouts and cancellation with AbortController
when: Requests or tasks can hang forever, the UI waits without end, or the user wants a cancel button.

title: Write user facing error messages
when: The app shows raw errors, vague text like "Something went wrong", or the user wants clearer error and validation messages.

title: Fix z-index and stacking context problems
when: A dropdown, tooltip, sticky header or modal shows behind other content even with a huge z-index.

title: Turn a vague bug report into clear repro steps
when: Someone reported a bug in vague words and it must be confirmed, narrowed down and written up so a developer can fix it.

title: Cross browser check with web standards
when: The user wants a page or app checked so it works in all current browser engines, using standards and fallbacks, not hacks.

title: Edge cases for dates and time zones
when: A feature handles dates, times, schedules, deadlines or ages, and the user wants it tested for date and time zone bugs.

title: Edge cases for empty and huge data
when: A list, table, chart or file processor needs testing with no data, a single item, and very large amounts of data.

title: Edge case hunt for user inputs
when: The user wants to find inputs that break a feature: text fields, search boxes, number fields, uploads or command line arguments.

title: Edge cases for numbers and money
when: A feature computes prices, totals, taxes, discounts, percentages or quantities, and the user wants it tested for numeric bugs.

title: Edge cases for unicode and international text
when: An app stores, searches, sorts, counts or shows user text, and the user wants it tested with accents, emoji, other scripts and right to left text.

title: Exploratory testing charter and session
when: The user wants unscripted testing that finds bugs a plan would miss, timeboxed and documented.

title: End to end form check
when: A form is built and the user wants it checked from first focus to final confirmation, including errors, success and what is saved or sent.

title: Game logic check with unit tests
when: A game has rules, scoring, collisions or randomness, and the user wants its logic verified by reading the code and testing pure functions.

title: Keyboard only QA pass
when: The user wants a page or app tested using only the keyboard: tab order, focus visibility, menus, dialogs and custom widgets.

title: Broken link and missing asset check
when: The user wants every link, image, script, stylesheet and font reference in a site checked for broken paths.

title: Performance budget check
when: The user has, or wants, size and request limits for a page or app and wants the build measured against them.

title: Persistence check after reload
when: An app saves state (notes, cart, settings, progress) and the user wants proof it survives reloads, other tabs, blocked storage and bad data.

title: Regression checklist after a change
when: After a fix or new feature, the user wants to make sure existing behavior did not break.

title: Final release sign off
when: Everything is said to be done and the user wants a final go or no go decision before shipping or handing over.

title: Responsive QA at standard widths
when: The user wants a built page checked at phone, tablet and desktop widths for layout bugs, overflow and readability.

title: Accessibility review pass
when: The user asks to check a page or app for accessibility problems against WCAG 2.2 AA and wants a report of what fails.

title: Review interface and page copy
when: The user wants the text of a page or app checked: spelling, grammar, clarity, consistent terms and tone, and leftover filler.

title: CSS stylesheet review
when: The user wants a stylesheet reviewed for maintainability, responsiveness, accessible styling and dead or conflicting rules.

title: Data migration review
when: A change alters saved data (a localStorage shape, a JSON file format, a SQL schema or CSV columns) and the migration needs review.

title: Review a new dependency before adding it
when: Someone wants to add a third party file, package or snippet, and the user wants it judged against using the platform.

title: Error handling review
when: The user wants code reviewed for how it fails: exceptions, rejected promises, bad files, network or storage errors, and what users see.

title: HTML markup review
when: The user wants HTML pages checked for valid structure, semantics, metadata and accessible markup before shipping.

title: Internationalization review
when: The user wants an app or site reviewed for readiness to translate and to serve other locales and languages.

title: JavaScript code review
when: The user asks to review JavaScript (browser scripts or shared modules) for bugs, risky patterns and readability before merging.

title: Logging review for scripts and servers
when: The user wants logs reviewed: useful when something breaks, quiet otherwise, and free of secrets and personal data.

title: Node HTTP server code review
when: The user wants a Node server or API built on node:http and the standard library reviewed for correctness, safety and robustness.

title: Performance review pass
when: The user says a page or app feels slow, or wants it reviewed for load and runtime performance before release.

title: Pull request size and scope review
when: A change set looks large or mixes unrelated work, and the user wants it checked for scope, size and reviewability.

title: Python script code review
when: The user wants a Python script or small module (standard library only) reviewed for bugs, error handling and clarity.

title: Security review pass
when: The user asks to check code for security problems: injection, XSS, leaked secrets, unsafe file access or weak input handling.

title: Test suite quality review
when: The user wants existing tests reviewed: do they test behavior, would they catch bugs, are they reliable and readable.

title: Screen reader smoke test
when: The user wants a quick check of how a page sounds with a screen reader: names, headings, landmarks, forms and live updates.

title: Bug severity and priority triage
when: There is a list of bugs or QA findings and the user wants them ranked so the most important get fixed first.

title: Smoke test right after a release
when: A new version was just published or packaged and the user wants a fast check that the critical paths work.

title: Test plan for an HTTP API
when: The user wants a plan to test an HTTP API or local server: endpoints, status codes, bodies, errors and limits.

title: Test plan for a form
when: The user wants test cases for a form (contact, sign up, checkout, booking, settings), including validation and submission.

title: Test plan for a browser game
when: The user wants a plan to test a small browser game: rules, controls, scoring, win and lose, pause and performance.

title: Test plan for a web page or site
when: Before or after building a page or site, the user wants a written test plan listing what to check, where and how.

title: Verify acceptance criteria one by one
when: A task is reported done and each acceptance criterion must be checked against the actual files, not assumed.

title: Visual QA of spacing and alignment
when: A built page or screen looks slightly off and the user wants a visual pass on alignment, spacing, sizes and consistency.

title: Architect: reviewing an existing code structure
when: A workspace already has code and the architect must judge its structure before new work is added on top.

title: Architect: checking a design against crew constraints
when: A proposed design or plan may need things the crew cannot use: packages, a build step, a remote service, a database server.

title: Architect: sketching data flow
when: An app has state that moves between input, storage and screen, and the team needs to agree where each value lives and how it changes.

title: Architect: interface contracts between files
when: Several workers write files that call each other (markup and script, modules, data and renderer) and must agree on names first.

title: Architect: file structure for a static site
when: The architect sets up where files live for a static site or small web app before the developers start writing.

title: Designer: design QA pass on built pages
when: Pages are built and the designer checks that the result matches the spec and looks right at phone and desktop widths.

title: Designer: choosing a look from the brief
when: The brief gives a subject and maybe a feeling (cozy, serious, playful) but no visual direction, and the designer must choose one.

title: Designer: polishing an existing page
when: A page works but looks plain or messy, and the user wants it to look more professional without changing the content.

title: Designer: handing off design tokens
when: The designer sets the visual values once so every developer and page uses the same colors, type and spacing.

title: Designer: visual spec for the developer
when: A task passes through the Design room first and the designer must write a spec that the developer turns into markup and styles.

title: Developer: finishing within a few turns
when: The developer runs on a small model with a limited number of turns and must finish the task without wandering.

title: Developer: read before edit, patch small
when: The developer must change a file that already exists, from a fix request, a QA finding or a new feature on old code.

title: Developer: self check before calling done
when: The developer believes the task is complete and is about to call done.

title: Developer: writing test.mjs with node:assert
when: The developer writes logic (calculation, parsing, filtering, state changes) and must leave a test that runs with plain node.

title: Developer: working with an unclear task
when: The task detail is ambiguous or contradicts the files, and the developer must still deliver something correct.

title: Ops: backup and rollback plan
when: A change could damage files or data (bulk edits, migrations, deletes, a new version replacing an old one) and must be undoable.

title: Ops: checking the environment before work
when: Before running or testing a project, ops confirms the machine has what it needs, or a run failed and the environment is suspect.

title: Ops: reading logs to triage a failure
when: A script, server or test run failed or behaves oddly, and ops must read the output or log files to find what to fix and who should fix it.

title: Ops: release checklist for a small project
when: A project is ready for a version (first release or an update) and ops must make sure nothing is missing before it is handed over.

title: Ops: running commands safely with approval
when: The ops worker must run shell commands (start a server, run tests, copy files) in the user workspace, where each run may need approval.

title: QA: using the automatic check results
when: QA receives the results of the automatic checks with the work and must turn them into findings correctly.

title: QA: testing each acceptance criterion
when: QA receives finished work and must decide, criterion by criterion, whether it meets what was asked.

title: QA: writing findings with severity and fix
when: QA has found problems and must write them so the developer can fix each one in a single pass.

title: QA: re checking a fix round
when: Work comes back to QA after fixes for earlier findings, and QA must confirm them without starting over.

title: QA: calibrating severity
when: QA must rate findings so the crew fixes what matters and the job is not blocked by taste.

title: Reviewer: writing constructive comments
when: The reviewer writes comments that another agent (often a small model) must understand and act on.

title: Reviewer: reviewing a diff
when: A task arrives in the Review room and the reviewer reads the changed files against the task and its criteria.

title: Reviewer: reviewing a fix round
when: A task returns to Review after its author fixed the issues from the last review.

title: Reviewer: catching scope creep
when: A diff contains more than the task asked: new features, refactors of untouched code, renamed files, extra dependencies.

title: Reviewer: approve or request changes
when: The reviewer has comments and must decide whether the task moves on to Test or goes back to its author.

title: Writer: page copy from a brief
when: The writer gets a short brief and must produce the real text for a page: headline, sections, buttons, footer.

title: Writer: a consistent docs voice
when: The writer writes or edits docs (README, guides, help pages) and must keep one clear voice across them.

title: Writer: editing text for clarity
when: Existing text (page copy, README, help) is long, vague or confusing, and the writer must make it clear without changing its facts.

title: Writer: microcopy for buttons and errors
when: An interface needs its small texts written: button labels, field hints, errors, empty states, confirmations and success messages.

title: Writer: writing text ready for translation
when: The text will be translated (a bilingual site, an app with a language switch) and must be written so translation is easy and safe.

title: Browser app structure with ES modules
when: The user wants a small web app split into clean files, asks how to organize JavaScript, or one script has grown too long to manage.

title: Canvas 2D drawing and animation loop
when: The user wants animated graphics, a simple game, particles, a drawing pad or a visualization drawn on a canvas.

title: INI and simple YAML config files
when: A script must read settings from an INI file or a simple YAML style file without third party parsers.

title: Theme tokens with CSS custom properties
when: The user wants consistent colors and spacing, a theme switch, dark mode, or to recolor a whole site by changing a few values.

title: Page layout with CSS grid and flexbox
when: The user needs columns, a sidebar layout, a card grid, centering or a footer that stays at the bottom, or a layout that breaks on small screens.

title: Event delegation for dynamic lists
when: A list, table or grid gets items added and removed at runtime and every item needs clicks, edits or keys handled.

title: Reordering items with the HTML drag and drop API
when: Items in a list or grid must be reordered or moved between groups by dragging (playlists, priorities, photo order), with a keyboard alternative.

title: Configuration from environment variables
when: An app or script needs ports, paths, keys or feature switches that change per machine, or reads settings scattered through the code.

title: Fetch with timeout, abort and error handling
when: The code calls an API or loads JSON with fetch and needs timeouts, cancellation, retries or clear error messages.

title: Geolocation with permission handling
when: The app needs the user position (near me search, distance, check in, local weather) and must handle permission and errors.

title: Semantic HTML document skeleton
when: The user wants a starting HTML file or boilerplate, or asks to fix the structure of a page so it uses semantic elements and landmarks.

title: IndexedDB storage wrapper with promises
when: The app stores more than localStorage should hold (many records, blobs, files) or needs indexed queries in the browser.

title: IntersectionObserver for reveal, lazy load and scroll spy
when: Something must happen when an element enters the viewport: reveal on scroll, load more items, highlight the current section, pause media.

title: JSON file as a small database with atomic writes
when: A Node app must persist a modest amount of data (up to a few thousand records) without a database server.

title: JSON Schema for a data or config format
when: The user wants to define or document the exact shape of a JSON file, API payload or config so others can produce and check it.

title: Makefile as a task runner
when: The user wants short commands such as make test or make run for a project, or a Makefile that rebuilds outputs only when sources change.

title: Running external commands from Node safely
when: A Node script must run other programs (git, a compiler, an image tool), capture their output or chain several commands.

title: Node command line tool with parseArgs and --help
when: The user wants a command line tool in Node with flags, positional arguments, a help screen and proper exit codes.

title: CORS headers and preflight in node:http
when: A page on one origin calls an API on another (other port or domain) and requests fail with a CORS error, or the API must allow chosen sites.

title: File watcher that reruns a task on change
when: The user wants a script that rebuilds, copies, tests or reloads automatically whenever files in a folder change.

title: Node script that processes a folder of files
when: The user wants a Node script that reads, renames, converts, sorts or summarizes many files in a folder.

title: JSON CRUD API with node:http
when: The user wants a small backend or REST API in Node with create, read, update and delete over JSON, without frameworks.

title: Rate limiting for a node:http server
when: A Node API or form endpoint needs protection from floods, brute force logins, or a client calling too often.

title: Interactive terminal prompts with readline
when: The user wants a Node program that asks questions, shows a menu, or runs a small text game or setup wizard in the terminal.

title: Scheduled jobs with timers in Node
when: A Node process must run a task every few minutes, daily at a set time, or retry later, without an external scheduler.

title: Live updates with server sent events
when: A page must update live from the server (progress, logs, notifications, a feed) and data only flows from server to client.

title: Static file server with safe paths
when: The user needs a tiny local server for a folder (to test modules or a service worker) or static serving inside a Node backend.

title: Streaming large files in Node
when: A script must read, transform or write files too big for memory (logs, exports, CSV with millions of rows), or compress them.

title: Test suite with node:test and node:assert
when: The user wants tests for a JavaScript project, a test command that needs no installs, or a regression test for a bug fix.

title: package.json scripts for a dependency free project
when: A Node project needs a package.json, consistent commands to start, develop and test, or the user asks how to run the project.

title: Password hashing with crypto.scrypt
when: A Node app stores user passwords or PINs and must hash them, or the code compares passwords in plain text.

title: Installable web app: manifest and install button
when: The user wants the site to be installable as an app, with an icon, a name and its own window.

title: Python command line tool with argparse
when: The user wants a Python script with options, subcommands, a help screen and exit codes, using only the standard library.

title: Reading and writing CSV in Python
when: A Python script must read, clean, filter or write CSV files, including exports from spreadsheet programs.

title: Data models with Python dataclasses
when: Python code passes dicts or tuples of related fields around, or the user wants clean model classes with defaults and validation.

title: Python backend with http.server
when: The user wants a small backend or local API in Python without frameworks, for example to serve data to a web page.

title: Logging setup for Python scripts and services
when: A Python program uses print for diagnostics, or needs log files, levels, or a --verbose flag.

title: Python file processing with pathlib
when: The user wants a Python script that finds, sorts, renames, copies or summarizes files in folders.

title: Text processing in Python with re
when: A Python script must extract, clean, split or replace patterns in text, such as dates in notes, codes in reports or emails in a document.

title: Python tests with unittest
when: The user wants tests for Python code using only the standard library, or a bug fix that needs a regression test.

title: HTTP client in Python with urllib.request
when: A Python script must call an HTTP API or download a file using only the standard library.

title: Python project setup: venv and requirements
when: A Python project needs setup instructions or a requirements file, or the user asks how to run the code on a fresh machine.

title: Writing and testing regular expressions
when: The user needs a regular expression in JavaScript to validate, find or replace text, or an existing regex misbehaves.

title: Offline support with a service worker
when: The user wants a site or app to open without a connection, or to cache its files for fast repeat visits.

title: Safe shell scripts with strict mode
when: The user wants a shell script for setup, backup or batch tasks, or an existing script breaks on spaces or keeps going after errors.

title: Portable SQL schema and queries
when: The user needs SQL tables, queries, joins or reports that should run on common relational databases without vendor features.

title: Hand written SVG icons and graphics
when: The page needs icons, a simple logo, badges or decorative drawings without image files or icon fonts.

title: Sound with the Web Audio API

title: Reusable Web Component (custom element)

when: The page freezes during a long calculation (parsing big files, image processing, search indexing, simulations).

when: The user wants a list that shows a first batch and loads more items on a button press or near the end of the scroll.

title: Modal dialog with the native dialog element
when: The user wants a modal window: a confirmation, a short form or a message that blocks the page until answered.

title: Multi step form wizard with progress
when: The user wants a long form split into steps with Next and Back buttons and a progress indicator.

title: Responsive navigation bar with menu toggle
when: The user wants a site header with a logo and links that collapses into a menu button on small screens.

title: Notification center with unread count
when: The user wants a bell button with an unread count that opens a panel listing recent notifications.

title: Off-canvas side drawer and bottom sheet
when: The user wants a panel that slides in from the side, such as a cart, filters or settings, without leaving the page.

title: Pagination links
when: The user wants page number links for a long list of results, posts or products.

title: Popover panel with the popover attribute
when: The user wants a small floating panel attached to a button that can hold links, buttons or a short form, without blocking the page.

title: Progress bar and loading spinner
when: The user wants to show progress of a task, such as an upload or a long operation, or a spinner while something loads.

title: Quantity stepper with minus and plus buttons
when: The user wants a number field with minus and plus buttons, such as product quantity in a cart or guests in a booking.

title: Radio cards and checkbox groups
when: The user wants options shown as selectable cards or grouped checkboxes, such as plan choice, shipping method or interests.

title: Range slider with value readout
when: The user wants a slider to choose a number or a min and max range, such as a price filter, volume or budget.

title: Share button with Web Share API and fallback
when: The user wants a Share button that opens the native share sheet on phones and offers simple options elsewhere.

title: Collapsible sidebar navigation for an app
when: The user wants a vertical app or dashboard sidebar with sections, icons and a way to collapse it.

title: Site footer with link groups and contact
when: The user wants the footer for a site: grouped links, contact details, social profiles and the legal line.

title: Skeleton loading screens
when: The user wants grey shapes that show the layout of content while it loads, instead of a spinner.

title: Sortable data table
when: The user wants a table of records whose columns can be sorted, and maybe filtered, that still works on phones.

title: Star rating input and display
when: The user wants people to rate something from 1 to 5 stars, or to show an average rating.

title: Stats strip with count up numbers
when: The user wants a row of big numbers with labels, such as clients served or years in business, maybe animated.

title: Sticky mobile call to action bar
when: The user wants a bar fixed to the bottom of phone screens with one or two actions, such as Call and Book.

title: Accessible tabs with keyboard support
when: The user wants content split into tabs that switch panels in place, such as specs, reviews and shipping.

title: Tag chips input
when: The user wants a field where typed words become removable chips, such as tags, skills, emails or keywords.

title: Testimonials block with quotes
when: The user wants a section of customer quotes or reviews to build trust.

title: Toast notifications with a live region
when: The user wants small temporary messages such as Saved, Copied or Upload failed that appear in a corner and fade away.

title: Accessible toggle switch
when: The user wants on and off switches for settings such as notifications, dark mode or privacy options.

title: Toolbar with toggle buttons and roving focus
when: The user wants a row of tool buttons, such as bold, italic and align for an editor, or view and sort actions above a list.

title: Tooltip that works on hover, focus and touch
when: The user wants a short text hint that appears next to an icon button or term on hover and focus.

title: Tree view for nested items
when: The user wants an expandable tree of nested items, such as folders and files, categories or an outline.

title: Vertical timeline of milestones
when: The user wants a timeline of events, such as company history, a project roadmap or a career path.

title: Responsive video embed
when: The user wants a video on a page, either a local file or an embed from a video host, sized for every screen.

title: Community group or club site

title: Documentation site

title: Event or conference page
when: The user wants a page for a conference, meetup, workshop, festival or launch event.

title: Gym or fitness studio site

title: Hotel or guesthouse site
